issues.description: Global compute-table identifier mismatch: template_repository/dd.py defines the compute-table variable as `_CT = ComputeTable()` while template_repository/dd_simulation.py imports `CT` (no underscore) from .dd. The solution repository defines the compute-table variable as `CT = ComputeTable()`. Because the template exposes `_CT` but dd_simulation.py expects `CT`, importing or running dd_simulation.py will raise an ImportError (name not found) and block students from executing the provided simulator code. This inconsistency also deviates from the solution API where `CT` is the public name.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the compute-table identifier consistent across the template and solution. Preferred fix: rename the variable in template_repository/dd.py from `_CT` to `CT` (i.e., `CT = ComputeTable()`) so it matches the import in dd_simulation.py and the solution. Alternatively, add an explicit alias in template dd.py (e.g., `CT = _CT`) so both `CT` and `_CT` exist. Do not change dd_simulation.py to import `_CT` because the solution and public API use `CT` — align the template to the public name to avoid confusing students.
